theme: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

reports.title: Patricia Cleghorn
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

promises.quote: NHS England recently established an adult mental health programme which is taking a whole system approach comprising crisis, acute, and community/primary care work streams. The acute care work stream has been developed in response to a number of recommendations set out by the Commission on Acute Adult Psychiatric Care and The Five Year Forward View for Mental Health, and is particularly relevant to the concerns outlined in your report.
promises.summary: Establish adult mental health programme with acute care work stream to address lack of acute beds and risk assessment concerns

concerns.quote: availability of acute mental health beds means the most vulnerable people are being cared for in the community with limited resources and care
concerns.hazard: lack of acute mental health beds

concerns.quote: The deceased had repeatedly stated that she would end her life by taking an overdose
No formal risk assessment was undertaken and staff failed to appreciate what drugs she had available to her

reports.title: Yong Hong
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

concerns.quote: the observation regime advised by the GP was not implemented
no risk assessment was carried out prior to making the decision to return his call bell
concerns.hazard: lack of risk assessment before call bell return

concerns.quote: care home staff did not receive training in how to carry out risk assessments
concerns.hazard: lack of staff training in risk assessments

concerns.quote: no interpreter was sought in the meantime to assist with assessment of his needs
No further advice was Sought from the GP or other appropriate clinician and he was left in social isolation without any means to express his distress,
concerns.hazard: lack of further clinical advice and social isolation

concerns.quote: no risk assessment was conducted and no further Input from the GP waa sought
concerns.hazard: lack of risk assessment and GP input

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that a necessary risk assessment was not performed before a critical decision. The earlier case concerned medication availability, while the later case concerned GP input and call‑bell return.
links.earlier_quote: No formal risk assessment was undertaken and staff failed to appreciate what drugs she had available to her.
links.later_quote: (c) no risk assessment was carried out prior to making the decision to return his call bell.
links.promise_quote: We will take action with regards to managing the breach of policy The Senior Nurse for Professional Standards issued a formal practice alert on 12th September 2016 to registered and unregistered clinicians in our crisis and community teams to reinforce the requirements for: Clinical Risk Assessments regarding risk of self-harm and/or suicide; Risk Assessments with regard to medicines management and self-medication; Safe administration of medication as per current Medicines Code and NMC Code.
